subject: Game Theory
title: Platform Envelopment
description: A fast breakdown of Platform Envelopment for builders.

hook.text: Microsoft killed Netscape by bundling Explorer for free with Windows. Platform envelopment in action.

buildup.text: A dominant platform can enter an adjacent market by bundling the new product with its existing one.

discovery.text: The attacker leverages its installed base. Users get the new product 'for free'—no reason to use the rival.

twist.text: Apple enveloped music players (iPod), maps (Apple Maps), and payments (Apple Pay) into the iPhone.

climax.text: Envelopment is why startups fear competing with tech giants—any successful product can be bundled away.

punchline.text: Bundle it, and the standalone dies.

quiz.question: What is platform envelopment?
options: Bundling a rival's product into your platform for free
